assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong, controllable light-matter coupling available on a chip: dispersive readout, cavity-mediated coupling and quantum-limited control of artificial atoms. It opened a new regime of microwave quantum optics and became the working platform for superconducting processors. It is distinct from the macroscopic tunnelling work recognised in 2025, though that prize clearly adjoins it.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) support a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Blais is the theory anchor and Wallraff and Schoelkopf are the experimental leads. Co-authors such as Girvin and Majer, and the roles of Nakamura and Devoret in related circuit work, mean the three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in dozens of laboratories over twenty years and underlying essentially all superconducting-qubit work, so confirmation is exceptional. Timing is good, but a prize so soon after 2025 may be judged too close in subject matter.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may weigh against it in committee judgment.
Fair division of credit among the many contributors to circuit QED is unresolved.
I work closely with this community and my assessment may be biased; I am unable to independently verify priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant, and the realisation of topological insulators, opened a new classification of band insulators with protected edge and surface states. Its conceptual originality is high and it has had lasting impact on materials and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposals, and Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe/CdTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's ARPES observation of 3D topological insulators is also a decisive contribution, and Bernevig, Zhang and Moore are not on the credited list. Any three-person split leaves unresolved claims; I am not an expert in this area.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent confirmation across many materials and techniques. Nobel recognition of topological phases (2016) is related but covers a different set of results.
uncertainties: Allocation between Molenkamp (2D, HgTe) and Hasan (3D, ARPES) is contested.
Contributions of Bernevig, Zhang and others are outside the credited names.
I defer to colleagues in materials physics on the fine details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable many-body quantum systems, from the superfluid to Mott insulator transition to quantum gas microscopy, and made quantum simulation a real experimental discipline. The tie to quantum information is strong and the physics is clean and tunable.
assessment.attribution: The credited list has five names; a defensible subset is Bloch (experimental programme), with Zoller and Cirac for the theoretical proposals. Greiner (Mott transition with Bloch and Hänsch) and Esslinger (fermionic Hubbard systems) are also strong and cannot be cleanly excluded. Overlap with Cirac and Zoller on the trapped-ion entry means one pair cannot honourably receive both.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely reproduced in many labs. Quantum simulation is a mature research tool, although the push for quantum advantage on practical problems remains ahead of us.
uncertainties: Selection among five credited names is hard and any subset omits major contributors.
Whether the contribution is best framed as the proposals or the experiments is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for a trapped-ion quantum computer and its experimental realisation brought controlled multi-qubit gates, entanglement and digital quantum simulation to a high level of fidelity. Trapped ions remain among the most accurate quantum platforms. Part of the field was recognised through Wineland's 2012 prize.
assessment.attribution: A theory-plus-experiment configuration with Cirac and Zoller on the proposal and Blatt on experimental realisation is plausible. Wineland's prior recognition, and the roles of Wineland, Monroe, Wineland-group gates and others, complicate the prize. Cirac and Zoller also appear in the optical-lattice entry.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed. Timeliness is reasonable, but the 2012 prize narrows the remaining uncovered ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for individual quantum systems.
Overlap in personnel with the optical-lattice entry.
Whether Blatt's contributions are decisive compared with Monroe and others not listed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in a tunable platform, and launched moiré materials as a field. The theoretical prediction of magic angles came before the experimental observation, giving a clear discovery narrative.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group's observations of correlated insulators and superconductivity are the clear core. Eva Andrei's experimental work on flat bands is also significant, and other theorists such as Kaxiras and Santos are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced by many groups since 2018 and still evolving. Some interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still open, so recognition could be seen as early, though it is clearly high-impact.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconductivity is not settled.
Credit for Andrei and for earlier theoretical work on twisted bilayers is open.
I am not a specialist in moiré materials.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade turned neutral atoms into programmable, strongly interacting qubit arrays, enabling quantum simulation and high-fidelity gates at scale. It is a major rival platform to superconducting circuits and has produced striking experiments in a short time.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Lukin provided the key theoretical proposal for Rydberg gates, and Lukin and Browaeys led some of the decisive experimental programmes. Saffman's contributions to blockade gates are also important, and the Harvard and Paris groups reached the arrays in parallel. A three-person selection is therefore contestable.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with independent groups reproducing results. Fault-tolerant claims are still being scrutinised, so it may be too early for a prize.
uncertainties: The field is still moving fast, so the final significance is uncertain.
Credit is contested among Lukin, Browaeys, Saffman and others.
Zoller's overlap with other entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical oscillators into the quantum regime, with ground-state cooling, strong coupling and quantum control of macroscopic motion. It has conceptual links to the macroscopic quantum behaviour recognised in 2025 and to quantum sensing, though it is more an enabling toolbox than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Kippenberg, Aspelmeyer and Painter are the leading experimentalists, but Vahala, Harris, Lehnert and Teufel also made decisive contributions to quantum control, and Teufel and Lehnert linked it with microwave circuits. Attribution in the field is clearly diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed experimentally and still developing. The compound structure of the field makes it hard to identify one discovery.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit among many groups.
The specific discovery to recognise is hard to define.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantized conductance in point contacts, discovered in 1988, is a fundamental result in mesoscopic physics showing the Landauer picture directly, and it remains a basic building block for quantum devices, including qubits and interferometers.
assessment.attribution: The two simultaneous 1988 papers (van Wees et al. in Delft and Wharam et al. at Cambridge) give a clear and unusual priority situation. Pepper led the Cambridge group and van Wees was first author in Delft; Landauer himself is deceased. A three-person prize is plausible but Wharam's role is less prominent.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and universally confirmed, but its recognition is long overdue and may now feel late relative to more recent discoveries.
uncertainties: Priority split between the Delft and Cambridge groups.
Whether the committee views a 1988 result as still a competitive proposal.
